He caught up with one protester who managed to avoid detention. "We were running back and forth. When the police are moving forward, we go back. When they are withdrawing, we are moving forward," the protester told DW. The protester described the heavy police presence as a "game of perception." "Where you have 20 protesters and 10 media persons, there are 100 police personnel standing. It seems like a joke, what they are doing with taxpayers' money," the protester said. Another protester, Jasmine, described how the morning unfolded for the demonstrators. "We have been playing a game of cat and mouse with the police, trying to stop them from picking us up," she said. "I don't think we have ever seen something like this happening. The journalists were later released. Newslaundry reported that police seized its reporters’ phones, while other reports said journalists were physically assaulted. The Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ), an independent nonprofit organization that promotes press freedom and defends journalists' rights worldwide, has called on Delhi Police to immediately release all detained journalists and media workers. It has also urged police to return their equipment, investigate reports of physical abuse, and allow the press to cover the ongoing protests in New Delhi and the police response without interference. In the 2026 World Press Freedom Index published by Reporters Without Borders (RSF), India ranked 157th out of 180 countries, down six places from 2025. Indian media reports said that Dipke's paternal grandmother had been suffering from a prolonged illness and had been unwell in recent days. It was now up to the CJP leader to decide whether to continue his protest while under detention or travel back for the funeral rites. This comes amid a reported crackdown on protesters attempting to reach the national capital, specifically central Delhi, to protest against India's chief election commissioner over alleged misconduct. Dharvi Vaid Dhulia Congress MP Shashi Tharoor has slammed the measures taken by Indian authorities to prevent the Cockroach Janta Party's protest from going ahead. He called out a "war-like deployment" of security personnel and said that the suspension of the internet in a key part of Delhi was among the "most regressive" and "repressive" measures. "A government confident in the fairness of its elections would welcome questions about them, whereas one that turns its capital into a fortress to avoid them only deepens the very suspicions it seeks to suppress. The government should provide answers, not lathis (sticks); expression, not repression," Tharoor wrote on X. He also called for the release of the protesters who had been detained. Tharoor said India's Gen Z "deserves better than an undeclared Emer-GenZ," in a play on words. Leaders of the CJP on Friday likened the clampdown on their planned protest to a "state of emergency." A state of emergency was declared in India by former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi in the mid-70s. Emergency powers were invoked by the Congress leader for 21 months, during which civil liberties were suspended, much of the opposition was jailed and media was censored. Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) National Convenor and former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal also mounted an emergency-related attack against Modi's government. "This is worse than the Emergency. It's official.. we are living under an absolute dictatorship ruled by Modi. "The Govt of India will deal strictly with the attempts you are making to incite tension, and BJP workers, remaining constantly among the people, will effectively thwart your designs," BJP President Nitin Nabin told news agencies on Saturday morning. "Your repeated electoral defeats in various states and the resulting desperation suggest that, in some way, you do not wish to see this country move forward peacefully. However, I warn you today that the BJP and the patriotic citizens of this country will give you a fitting and stern response," he said. Nabin suggested that "foreign forces" were behind the opposition leaders and that the protests were an attempt to "destabilize" India. BJP leaders have made similar claims before without offering proof.
